label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Subject: Re: Saturday alarm

Kristen,

It was my popcorn. Saturday, November 7, at about 10:40, I put a bag in the break room microwave, hit the popcorn button and walked out front. A guy needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and helping him took longer than I thought—probably six or seven minutes.

The store was cleared out for about 25 minutes, and the engine from up on Hertel came. There was no damage, just smoke and a terrible stink. This was on me, not the microwave. I’m sorry I left it unattended and put everyone out in the cold. I feel bad about the Hendersons leaving their cart, too. They’ll be back—they always are—but they shouldn’t have had to deal with that.

Just so it’s clear for Gary’s records, the September alarm wasn’t me. That was the sensor in the paint aisle.

One of the guys on the engine was Mikey Szymanski, who I broke in as a probie back in ’03. He’s never going to let me forget it. Thirty-one years on the job, and my first alarm as a civilian is over a bag of butter popcorn. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

I’ll cover the $175. You can take it out of my check or I can bring cash, whichever you prefer. And I’ll buy Denise her coffee.

I hope you’ll let me keep my Saturday shifts. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I understand the new rule, and there won’t be any more microwave popcorn from me.

Sorry again,
Walt
